ch8_arrival.speaker: narrator
ch8_arrival.text: The road into the village is the same road. The hills are the same hills. Nothing else is the same.

ch8_arrival.speaker: aline
ch8_arrival.text: It's so quiet. I used to think this village was never quiet.

ch8_aline.speaker: aline
ch8_aline.text: I'm here. Take as long as you need.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: Emmanuel. Aline. You came back. You both came back.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: Sit down, Emmanuel. Sit with me.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: Your father did not survive. They came back the morning after you left, as they said they would. He never told them where you had gone. Not one word.
ch8_beata.text_reduced: Your father did not survive. He never told them where you had gone.

ch8_beata.speaker: narrator
ch8_beata.text: Emmanuel does not hear what she says next. Aline takes his hand, and does not let go.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: There is someone here who has been waiting for you, Aline.

ch8_beata.speaker: narrator
ch8_beata.text: A boy steps out from behind the counter. He is thinner, and he is wearing one mended sandal. Aline is carrying the other.

ch8_beata.speaker: narrator
ch8_beata.text: A boy steps out from behind the counter, thinner than before, blinking at the light.

ch8_beata.speaker: olivier
ch8_beata.text: Mama Beata hid me in the roof. For weeks. I was very quiet, Aline. Like you told me.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: He was. Quieter than any of us.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: In the end I hid eleven people. In the roof, behind the sacks, under the floor of the storeroom. Madame Uwase was one of them. Not everyone I tried to hide lived.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: Some people have come out of the marsh these last weeks. Not all of them. We are still searching, every day, for the ones who were with you.

ch8_beata.speaker: beata
ch8_beata.text: Go and see the village, Emmanuel. Go to your father's house. Then come to the square. People are gathering there.

ch8_beata_after.speaker: beata
ch8_beata_after.text: Go on. I'll be in the square.

ch8_olivier.speaker: olivier
ch8_olivier.text: Aline says you looked for me. In the dark. Thank you, Emmanuel.

ch8_home.speaker: narrator
ch8_home.text: The door of Joseph's house hangs from one hinge. Inside, the cupboard still stands across the doorway of the storage room.

ch8_home.speaker: narrator
ch8_home.text: Emmanuel lays flowers on the step where his father used to sit in the evenings with the radio.

choices.text: "Quietly, and together. We did it the way you said."
[Sit on the step for a while.]

ch8_home.speaker: emmanuel
ch8_home.text: Not one word. Mama Beata said. You kept us all alive with silence.

ch8_home.speaker: emmanuel
ch8_home.text: We opened the door when someone knocked. Like you asked me to.

ch8_home.speaker: narrator
ch8_home.text: Emmanuel sits on the step for a long time. Aline sits beside him and says nothing at all.

ch8_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch8_uwase.text: Emmanuel. Mama Beata told me you were alive. I made her say it three times.

ch8_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch8_uwase.text: The school has no roof, no benches, no books. And so many of my pupils will never come back.

ch8_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch8_uwase.text: But the ones who do will need teachers. Two of us, perhaps.

ch8_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch8_uwase.text: Then we start with what is true. Children will have to learn it from us, not from a radio.

ch8_uwase.speaker: uwase
ch8_uwase.text: Nobody knows if they can. They do it anyway. That is what courage looks like most days.

ch8_uwase_after.speaker: uwase
ch8_uwase_after.text: Come back tomorrow. We'll start with the benches.

ch8_hill.speaker: narrator
ch8_hill.text: From the hilltop, the village looks almost the way it did. Almost.

ch8_hill.speaker: aline
ch8_hill.text: We survived. But survival isn't the same as healing.

ch8_hill.speaker: emmanuel
ch8_hill.text: Then we have to start healing. And remember those who didn't come home.

ch8_hill.speaker: aline
ch8_hill.text: Do you remember what you promised me? Up here?

ch8_hill.speaker: aline
ch8_hill.text: And I'll become a doctor. It's still a promise. It's still ours.

ch8_hill.speaker: aline
ch8_hill.text: So do I. That's why it hurts. That's why it matters.

ch8_ball.speaker: narrator
ch8_ball.text: The old football lies in the grass at the edge of the pitch, flat and split. Someone will need to find a new one. And a pump.

ch8_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch8_claudine.text: Eric has started talking again. Mostly about you, and the river. He says you were very brave and very wet.

ch8_eric.speaker: child
ch8_eric.text: Emmanuel! You still owe me a story. The hare and the hyena.

ch8_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch8_gasana.text: My beans have come up on their own, would you believe it? The field didn't know anything had happened. I'm going to need help with the sacks.

ch8_solange.speaker: solange
ch8_solange.text: My mother is alive. She's in a camp near the border. I leave tomorrow to bring her home.

ch8_innocent.speaker: innocent
ch8_innocent.text: My leg still aches when it rains. Every time it does, I think: someone stopped.

ch8_memorial.speaker: narrator
ch8_memorial.text: In the square, people have started to gather stones. A low wall, flowers, candles in tins. Names written on scraps of paper, held down with pebbles.

ch8_memorial.speaker: beata
ch8_memorial.text: Rebuilding takes more than walls. It takes patience, truth, and people willing to stand beside each other.

ch8_memorial.speaker: emmanuel
ch8_memorial.text: I will teach. I will tell their stories. I will not let hatred be the lesson.

ch8_memorial.speaker: narrator
ch8_memorial.text: Emmanuel writes his father's name on a scrap of paper. Joseph. He holds it down with a stone from the yard where Joseph would not open the gate.

ch8_memorial.speaker: narrator
ch8_memorial.text: Beside it, Aline writes another name. Gasana. He lived through the river; the fever took him weeks later, in the camp.

ch8_memorial.speaker: narrator
ch8_memorial.text: And another, for the man beside the path who thought no one would stop. Innocent. His brother never came back for him.

ch8_memorial.speaker: aline
ch8_memorial.text: What will you do now, Emmanuel? Tomorrow. Where do we start?

choices.text: "Homes, for the families who come back."
"A garden here, around the names, so they are never alone."

ch8_memorial.speaker: beata
ch8_memorial.text: Then begin tomorrow. And not alone.
